behavior_items: The reproducer is a minimal binary crate targeting edition 2021 and pinned to nightly-2024-10-15, which indicates it is intended to exercise a nightly rustc regression or ICE rather than stable language behavior.

The call to `std::arch::x86_64::_mm_shuffle_ps` exercises the x86_64 architecture-specific SIMD intrinsic interface from `std::arch`. Both vector operands are written as `todo!()`. The `todo!()` macro expands to an expression of the never type `!`, which can coerce to any required type. Checks the fields of a struct literal against the chosen variant: it reconciles expectation-derived hints with the ADT type, tracks remaining and duplicate fields, resolves each supplied field, records field indices, validates stability and field types, reports unknown fields, checks field expressions with hints/coercions, registers well-formedness obligations, and emits diagnostics for missing fields or FRU-related mistakes. This method calls the listed methods `expected_inputs_for_expected_output`, `demand_eqtype`, `write_field_index`, `field_ty`, `report_unknown_field`, `check_expr_with_hint`, `demand_coerce_diag`, and `suggest_fru_from_range_and_emit`.
Performs error-recovery checking for struct literal contents by still type-checking every explicit field expression and the optional base expression. This method calls the listed method `check_expr`.

Builds and emits the missing-fields diagnostic for a struct literal, formatting a readable list of omitted fields and, when there is at least one written field, delegating to a FRU typo suggestion path before emission. This method calls the listed method `suggest_fru_from_range_and_emit`.

Detects the common typo where a range literal was written where functional record update syntax was likely intended, attaches a targeted FRU subdiagnostic and suppresses conflicting range-type errors when applicable, otherwise emitting the original error directly. It does not call other listed methods.

Reports that a struct literal cannot be constructed because of private fields, distinguishing explicitly used versus merely remaining private fields, labeling or noting them, and searching inherent impl items for constructor-like associated functions whose signatures match the ADT so it can suggest alternatives. It does not call other listed methods.

Emits the diagnostic for using an unknown field in a struct/variant literal, tailoring the message for enum variants vs other ADTs, suggesting tuple-style constructor syntax for tuple variants, and offering likely field-name corrections based on available visible fields. This method calls the listed methods `available_field_names` and `name_series_display`.

Collects suggestable field names from a variant, excluding fields already present in `skip_fields` and filtering through field-suggestability checks. This method calls the listed method `is_field_suggestable`.
Formats a bounded, human-readable comma-separated series of field names, appending an `... and N others` suffix when the list is longer than the display limit. It does not call other listed methods.

Recursively searches a non-enum ADT, including nested unnamed fields, for a field matching the given identifier, pushing the discovered access path into `nested_fields` and returning whether a match was found. This method calls the listed method `find_adt_field` recursively.

Type-checks field access by checking and resolving the base expression, autodereferencing through candidate receiver types, locating direct or nested ADT fields, recording field indices, applying deref adjustments and obligations for accessible fields, handling tuple indexing syntax, and otherwise reporting private or nonexistent-field errors. This method calls the listed methods `check_expr`, `find_adt_field`, `field_ty`, `write_field_index`, `ban_private_field_access`, and `ban_nonexisting_field`.

When the base type is an `impl Future`, checks whether the requested field exists on the future's `Output` type and, if so, suggests inserting `.await`; otherwise it just labels the field as unknown. It does not call other listed methods.

Builds and emits the main diagnostic for accessing a nonexistent field, specializing suggestions for arrays, raw pointers, type parameters, and opaque futures, then trying a method-call suggestion if calling the base expression would yield a type with the requested field, and adding the Rust-2018 `.await` note when relevant. This method calls the listed methods `no_such_field_err`, `maybe_suggest_array_indexing`, `suggest_first_deref_field`, `point_at_param_definition`, and `suggest_await_on_field_access`.

Emits the private-field-access diagnostic and, when appropriate, suggests calling an accessible method with the same name instead of reading the field. This method calls the listed method `private_field_err`.

Reports the error for treating a method as a field value, then suggests either removing wrapping parentheses for an accidental call pattern, adding call parentheses, or dereferencing first for raw-pointer-to-ADT cases where the field exists after dereference. It does not call other listed methods.

Augments a diagnostic for field access on a type parameter by locating the non-synthetic type parameter declaration in the current body and labeling where that parameter was introduced. It does not call other listed methods.

For mistaken tuple-style field syntax on arrays, labels the field as unknown and, when the field parses as an integer and the array length is evaluable, suggests rewriting `.n` as `[n]` with an applicability tuned by bounds confidence. It does not call other listed methods.
For raw-pointer field access, labels the field as unknown and suggests wrapping the base expression in an explicit dereference before accessing the field. It does not call other listed methods.

Constructs the base `no field` diagnostic and enriches it with suggestions for nested-field access paths, misspelled field names, and visible candidate field listings; it also unwraps `Option`/`Result`-like outer types when searching for nested matches. This method calls the listed methods `get_field_candidates_considering_privacy`, `check_for_nested_field_satisfying`, and `name_series_display`.
Constructs the base diagnostic for accessing a private field, naming the enclosing item and labeling the offending field span. It does not call other listed methods.

Type-checks indexing expressions by checking both operands, resolving the base type, using normal indexing lookup when available, coercing the index to the required index type and retargeting obligation spans, otherwise probing for a nearly applicable `Index` impl with unsatisfied predicates, and finally emitting specialized diagnostics for non-indexable types such as tuples or pointers. This method calls the listed methods `check_expr`, `lookup_indexing`, `point_at_index`, and `find_and_report_unsatisfied_index_impl`.

When normal indexing lookup fails, probes for exactly one relevant `Index` impl, instantiates it in a speculative obligation context, equates its self type with the base type, registers and selects its predicates/projection obligations, and reports fulfillment errors if only nested obligations are preventing the impl from applying. It does not call other listed methods.

Post-processes fulfillment errors from indexing so diagnostics point at the index expression span, tracking `Index`/`SliceIndex`-related predicates to retarget only the relevant obligations without duplicating unrelated diagnostics. It does not call other listed methods.

Checks a `yield` expression against the current coroutine context. If coroutine types are available, it calls `check_expr_coercible_to_type` to coerce the yielded value to the coroutine's `yield_ty` and returns the coroutine `resume_ty`. Otherwise it emits an error through `dcx().emit_err`, calls `check_expr` on the yielded value to ensure it is still type-checked, and returns `unit`.

Checks one inline-assembly operand, using `check_expr_with_needs` to type-check the expression with either no place requirement for inputs or mutable-place requirement for outputs, then `require_type_is_sized` to enforce `Sized`. For non-inputs it rejects non-place expressions via `dcx().struct_span_err(...).emit()`. For inputs it calls `structurally_resolve_type` and, when the resolved type is a function item or reference, uses `demand_coerce` to coerce it respectively to a function pointer or raw pointer.

Checks an entire inline `asm!` expression and determines whether it yields `!` or `()`. It calls `check_expr_asm_operand` for each input/output operand, and for label operands it calls `check_block_with_expected` with unit expectation, then uses `demand_suptype` to require `()` when the label block does not diverge. It also restores divergence tracking for label blocks and returns `never` if the asm is guaranteed not to return, otherwise `unit`.

Checks an `offset_of` expression by lowering the container type with `lower_ty`, repeatedly resolving the current container with `structurally_resolve_type`, and walking the requested field path while validating enum variants, tuple fields, and struct fields. Along the way it emits feature and lookup diagnostics, calls `require_type_is_sized` for field types and `require_type_has_static_alignment` for the overall container, checks field visibility/stability, and accumulates the resolved field indices for the final offset computation.

Determines whether evaluating a place expression is guaranteed to perform a read when handling `!`; non-place expressions are treated as reads immediately, while specific parent-expression contexts such as address-of, field projection, and assignment LHS are exempted. For `match` and `let` parents, it calls `pat_guaranteed_to_constitute_read_for_never` to decide based on the corresponding pattern(s).

Determines whether a pattern match against a `!`-typed value is guaranteed to constitute a read. It recursively calls `pat_guaranteed_to_constitute_read_for_never` on each subpattern of an `Or` pattern and otherwise classifies wildcard as non-reading, `Never` as reading, and all remaining pattern forms as reading.

Enforces that a non-constant array repeat element type satisfies the `Copy` lang-item requirement, while exempting actual constants and const blocks and annotating whether the element could be extracted into a const for diagnostics. It calls `node_ty` to inspect call targets, `require_lang_item` to obtain `Copy`, and `require_type_meets` to register the obligation.

Collects autoderef-reachable non-enum ADT fields that are accessible and suggestable for diagnostics, skipping probing if autoderef hits the recursion limit and ignoring types whose fields are all private. It calls `autoderef` to build the deref chain and `is_field_suggestable` to filter the returned field candidates.

Searches recursively, up to depth three, for a field path whose field and instantiated type satisfy a diagnostic predicate, starting from a candidate field and descending through nested accessible fields. It calls `get_field_candidates_considering_privacy_for_diag` to enumerate nested field candidates and recursively calls `check_for_nested_field_satisfying_condition_for_diag` to continue the search.
method_docs.compiler/rustc_hir_typeck/src/callee.rs:: Validates that a trait may be invoked via method-call syntax in the current body, with a special rejection for explicit `Drop` destructor calls outside the fallback drop surface; if allowed, it forces coherence checking via `coherent_trait`. This method does not call other listed file methods.

Main entry point for checking a call expression: type-checks the callee, resolves its type, walks autoderef steps, and selects a call strategy. It calls `try_overloaded_call_step` while probing, then dispatches to `confirm_builtin_call`, `confirm_deferred_closure_call`, or `confirm_overloaded_call` depending on the chosen `CallStep`, and finally registers a well-formedness obligation for the return type.

Examines one autoderef stage to determine how the callee can be invoked. It recognizes direct builtin callable types, records deferred resolution for closures or coroutine-closures whose callable kind is still unknown, and otherwise attempts trait-based dispatch by calling `try_overloaded_call_traits`; on success it prepares adjustments and returns the corresponding `CallStep`.

Searches the `Fn*` and `AsyncFn*` trait families for a callable method applicable to the adjusted callee type, preferring trait order based on whether the callee is a coroutine closure. It computes the tupled argument input type, performs trait-method lookup, registers resulting obligations, and returns any needed autoref adjustment plus the selected `MethodCallee`. This method does not call other listed file methods.

Detects the parser pattern where a block-bodied closure definition is immediately followed by call syntax without parentheses and emits a multipart suggestion to wrap the closure. It also handles the async-closure desugaring case when locating the real closure declaration span. This method does not call other listed file methods.

Recognizes a likely mistaken array element separator, where tuple-like syntax is being called inside an array literal, and suggests inserting a comma after the tuple expression. Returns whether the suggestion was emitted. This method does not call other listed file methods.

Finalizes checking of a direct builtin call on a function item or function pointer. It calls `enforce_context_effects` for `FnDef` callees, computes and normalizes the function signature, checks argument types against expected inputs, performs diagnostics for non-callable callees, and in the error path may call `suggest_call_as_method` and `report_invalid_callee`.

Builds a diagnostic suggestion that rewrites a failed free-function-style call into method-call syntax when method probing succeeds on the first argument. It probes and confirms a candidate method, then constructs a multipart source rewrite preserving precedence and optionally names the implementing trait. This method does not call other listed file methods.

Creates the main error for attempting to call a non-callable expression, with specialized suggestions for unit constructors, misplaced closure syntax, local function items, bad array syntax, multiline formatting, and unsized callees. It calls `identify_bad_closure_def_and_call` and `maybe_suggest_bad_array_definition` while refining diagnostics.

Checks arguments for a closure call whose exact callable trait kind has been deferred, using the known closure signature to derive expected input types and return type. It calls `check_argument_types` and returns the closure signature output.

Enforces that a called function's host-effect const parameter matches the effect expected for the current body. It equates the body effect with the callee's host-effect argument, registering obligations on success or emitting a mismatched-const diagnostic otherwise. This method does not call other listed file methods.

Finalizes an overloaded call resolved through a callable trait method. It calls `check_method_argument_types` to type-check the call against the selected `MethodCallee`, then calls `write_method_call_and_enforce_effects` to record the method call and enforce any context effects, returning the method output type.

Completes a previously deferred closure-call resolution once closure kind inference has finished. It calls `try_overloaded_call_traits` to pick the appropriate callable trait method, equates the old deferred signature with the resolved method signature, applies stored plus autoref adjustments, and calls `write_method_call_and_enforce_effects` to record the resolved method call.
method_docs.compiler/rustc_middle/src/ty/consts.rs::: Returns the cached type flags stored in the interned const wrapper by directly reading `self.0.flags`. It does not call other listed methods.
Returns the cached outer exclusive binder depth from the interned const wrapper via `self.0.outer_exclusive_binder`. It does not call other listed methods.
Returns the cached `ConstKind` of the interned constant from `self.0.kind`. It does not call other listed methods.
Returns the cached `TypeFlags` for the constant from `self.0.flags`. It does not call other listed methods.
Returns the constant's cached outer exclusive binder depth from `self.0.outer_exclusive_binder`. It does not call other listed methods.
Core constructor that interns a constant from a `ConstKind` and type using the type context. It calls `mk_ct_from_kind`.
Constructs a `ConstKind::Param` constant for a const parameter. It explicitly calls `Const::new`.
Constructs an inference-variable constant using `InferConst::Var`. It explicitly calls `Const::new`.
Constructs a fresh inference constant using `InferConst::Fresh`. It explicitly calls `Const::new`.
Constructs a constant from an arbitrary `InferConst`. It explicitly calls `Const::new`.
Constructs a bound constant with the given Debruijn index and bound variable. It explicitly calls `Const::new`.
Constructs a placeholder constant from a `PlaceholderConst`. It explicitly calls `Const::new`.
Constructs an unevaluated constant wrapper around `UnevaluatedConst`. It explicitly calls `Const::new`.
Constructs a value constant from a `ValTree`. It explicitly calls `Const::new`.
Constructs a constant expression node from `ty::Expr`. It explicitly calls `Const::new`.
Constructs an error sentinel constant carrying an already-reported error. It explicitly calls `Const::new`.
Builds a generic delayed-bug error constant for missing diagnostics. It explicitly calls `Const::new_error_with_message`.
Emits a delayed bug with the provided span and message, then wraps the reported error as a constant. It explicitly calls `dcx`, `span_delayed_bug`, and `Const::new_error`.

Lowers an HIR anonymous const into `ty::Const` by extracting its body and type, trying to eagerly convert literal/parameter forms, and otherwise producing an unevaluated const with identity args. It explicitly calls `hir_node_by_def_id`, `def_span`, `to_def_id`, `hir`, `body`, `type_of`, `no_bound_vars`, `expect`, `Const::try_from_lit_or_param`, `Const::new_unevaluated`, and `identity_for_item`.

Attempts to convert an HIR expression into an immediately usable constant by unwrapping trivial blocks, recognizing literals via `lit_to_const`, and special-casing const-parameter paths into param/bound/error constants as needed. It explicitly calls `is_empty`, `is_some`, `as_ref`, `unwrap`, `at`, `lit_to_const`, `dcx`, `span_delayed_bug`, `type_of`, `instantiate_identity`, `named_bound_var`, `parent`, `generics_of`, `item_name`, `Const::new_param`, `Const::new`, `Const::new_bound`, `from_u32`, and `Const::new_error`.

Constructs a value constant from raw integer bits by computing the target layout size and wrapping the bits as a scalar `ValTree`. It explicitly calls `layout_of`, `unwrap_or_else`, `Const::new_value`, `from_scalar_int`, `try_from_uint`, and `unwrap`.
Constructs the canonical zero-sized value constant for the given type. It explicitly calls `Const::new_value` and `zst`.
Constructs a boolean constant by forwarding to the raw-bits constructor with the builtin `bool` type. It explicitly calls `Const::from_bits`, `empty`, and `and`.
Constructs a target-`usize` constant by forwarding to the raw-bits constructor with the builtin `usize` type. It explicitly calls `Const::from_bits`, `empty`, and `and`.

Evaluates a constant to a `ValTree` when possible: unevaluated consts are prepared and resolved through type-checking const-eval, value consts are returned directly, error consts propagate their error, and param/infer/bound/placeholder/expr consts are rejected as too generic. It explicitly calls `has_escaping_bound_vars`, `Const::kind`, `prepare_for_eval`, `const_eval_resolve_for_typeck`, `dcx`, `span_delayed_bug`, and `into`.

Normalizes a constant by attempting evaluation and replacing it with a value constant or error constant when evaluation succeeds or reports an error; otherwise it leaves too-generic constants unchanged. It explicitly calls `Const::eval`, `Const::new_value`, `Const::ty`, `Const::new_error`, and `into`.

Evaluates the constant in the given type context and parameter environment and returns its scalar value if evaluation succeeds. It explicitly calls `eval` and then `try_to_scalar` on the evaluated constant.
Evaluates the constant to a scalar integer, returning `None` if evaluation or integer conversion fails. It explicitly calls `try_eval_scalar` and then converts the resulting scalar with `try_to_int`.

Evaluates the constant to raw bits by first obtaining a scalar integer and then interpreting it using the constant type's layout size. It explicitly calls `try_eval_scalar_int` and `self.ty()` from this methods list, while also querying `tcx.layout_of(...)` to determine the bit width.
Returns the evaluated raw bits of the constant, panicking with `bug!` if bit evaluation fails. It explicitly calls `try_eval_bits`, and uses `self.ty()` when formatting the failure message.
Evaluates the constant to a target-sized `usize` value if possible. It explicitly calls `try_eval_scalar_int` and then converts the result with `try_to_target_usize`.
Evaluates the constant to a boolean by first obtaining a scalar integer and then attempting a boolean conversion. It explicitly calls `try_eval_scalar_int`.
Returns the evaluated target-sized `usize` value of the constant, panicking with `bug!` if evaluation fails. It explicitly calls `try_eval_target_usize`.
Extracts the underlying `ValTree` from a constant known to have `ConstKind::Value`, panicking otherwise. It inspects the constant kind via `kind`.
Returns the underlying `ValTree` when the constant has `ConstKind::Value`, or `None` for other constant kinds. It inspects the constant kind via `kind`.
Attempts to extract a scalar value from the constant by first obtaining its `ValTree`. It explicitly calls `try_to_valtree`.
Attempts to extract a target-sized `usize` directly from the constant's structural value representation. It explicitly calls `try_to_valtree` and then delegates to the `ValTree` conversion.
Checks whether this constant is an inference constant. It inspects the constant kind via `kind` and matches `ConstKind::Infer`.

Retrieves the default value for a local const generic parameter from HIR and wraps it in an `EarlyBinder`. It explicitly calls `Const::from_anon_const` to lower the anonymous constant after locating the default const definition.
Returns the underlying `ConstKind` for this interned constant by directly calling `Const::kind` on `self`.
Trait shim that tries to extract this constant as a target-sized `u64` by directly calling `Const::try_to_target_usize`.
Trait constructor wrapper that creates an inference constant by directly calling `Const::new_infer`.
Trait constructor wrapper that creates a const variable by directly calling `Const::new_var`.
Trait constructor wrapper that creates a bound constant by directly calling `Const::new_bound`.
Trait constructor wrapper for anonymous bound constants that delegates to `Const::new_bound`; it explicitly calls `new_bound` rather than a distinct `new_anon_bound` constructor.
Trait constructor wrapper that creates an unevaluated constant by directly calling `Const::new_unevaluated`.
Trait constructor wrapper that creates a constant expression by directly calling `Const::new_expr`.
Trait constructor wrapper that creates an error sentinel constant by directly calling `Const::new_error`.

Lowers a HIR const argument into `Const`. For anonymous const args paired with `FeedConstTy::Param`, it feeds the inferred type with `tcx.feed_anon_const_type` using `tcx.type_of`. It then dispatches by kind: path arguments call `from_param`, while anonymous arguments call `from_anon_const`.

Converts a resolved HIR const-parameter path into the appropriate constant form. It queries `tcx.named_bound_var` and, for early-bound params, calls `tcx.parent`, `tcx.generics_of`, and `tcx.item_name` before constructing a param constant with `ty::Const::new_param`; for late-bound params it calls `ty::Const::new_bound` with `ty::BoundVar::from_u32`; for resolution errors it calls `ty::Const::new_error`.

Evaluates this constant into a `(Ty, ValTree)` pair when possible. It first asserts there are no escaping bound vars via `has_escaping_bound_vars`, then inspects the constant with `kind`. For `Unevaluated`, it calls `prepare_for_eval`, then `tcx.const_eval_resolve_for_typeck`, and on success computes the resulting type with `tcx.type_of(...).instantiate(...)`. `Value` returns directly, `Error` converts into an error result, and param/infer/bound/placeholder/expr forms return `TooGeneric`.
Tries to extract this constant as a boolean by chaining through `try_to_valtree`, then `try_to_scalar_int`, then scalar-int `try_to_bool`, finally converting the result with `ok()`.

Computes the valid coroutine state variant range from `FIRST_VARIANT` up to the number of layout variants. It calls `coroutine_layout`, `unwrap`, and `next_index`.
Builds the discriminant for a specific coroutine variant by asserting the variant is in range and using the variant index as the discriminant value. It calls `variant_range` and `discr_ty`.
Iterates over all coroutine variants and yields each variant paired with its implicit discriminant, whose value is the variant index. It calls `variant_range` and `discr_ty`.
Returns the display name for a coroutine variant, mapping reserved indices to fixed names and formatting other indices as `SuspendN`.
Returns the coroutine discriminant type, which is always `u32`.

Iterates over each coroutine variant and then over the stored field types for that variant, instantiating layout field types with the coroutine arguments. It calls `coroutine_layout`, `kind_ty`, `unwrap`, `bind`, and `instantiate`.
Returns the coroutine prefix types by delegating directly to the captured upvar types. It calls `upvar_tys`.

Extracts the individual captured upvar types for closures, coroutines, or coroutine closures by first obtaining the tupled upvars type and then unpacking its tuple fields. It calls `tupled_upvars_ty` on the underlying closure/coroutine/coroutine-closure args via `as_closure`, `as_coroutine`, or `as_coroutine_closure`, then calls `kind`, and for tuple cases calls this type's own `tupled_upvars_ty` and `tuple_fields`.

Returns the tuple type that represents all captured upvars for a closure, coroutine, or coroutine closure. It calls `as_closure`, `as_coroutine`, or `as_coroutine_closure`, and then the corresponding `tupled_upvars_ty`.
Constructs inline-const arguments by concatenating the inherited parent generic arguments with the synthetic trailing result type and interning the full argument list. It calls `mk_args_from_iter`.
Splits inline-const arguments into the parent argument slice and the final synthetic type argument, asserting that the synthetic argument is present.
Returns the inherited parent generic arguments for an inline const. It calls `split`.
Returns the synthetic result type stored in the inline-const arguments. It calls `split` and `expect_ty`.
Extracts the contained bound region kind, or bugs if the bound variable is not a region.
Extracts the contained bound type kind, or bugs if the bound variable is not a type.

Finds the source span of this type parameter within a given item's generics. It calls `generics_of`, `type_param`, and `def_span`.
Returns the index of the const parameter.
Constructs a `ParamConst` from its index and name.
Builds a `ParamConst` from a generic parameter definition. It calls `new`.

Returns the underlying bound variable index stored in this `BoundTy`.
Asserts that this bound type's kind matches the provided bound variable kind. It calls `expect_ty`.
Creates an anonymous `BoundTy` from a bound variable index.
Interns a `TyKind` into a `Ty` via the type context by calling `tcx.mk_ty_from_kind`.
Constructs an inference type by wrapping the given `InferTy` in `TyKind::Infer`; explicitly calls `Ty::new`.

Builds a type-variable inference `Ty`, reusing a pre-interned entry from `tcx.types.ty_vars` when available and otherwise constructing `Infer(TyVar(v))`; explicitly calls `Ty::new` on the fallback path.
Constructs an integer inference variable type; explicitly calls `Ty::new_infer` with `IntVar(v)`.
Constructs a floating-point inference variable type; explicitly calls `Ty::new_infer` with `FloatVar(v)`.
Builds a fresh type inference placeholder, reusing a pre-interned entry from `tcx.types.fresh_tys` when possible and otherwise creating one; explicitly calls `Ty::new_infer` on the fallback path.

Builds a fresh integer inference placeholder, reusing a pre-interned entry from `tcx.types.fresh_int_tys` when possible and otherwise creating one; explicitly calls `Ty::new_infer` on the fallback path.

Builds a fresh floating-point inference placeholder, reusing a pre-interned entry from `tcx.types.fresh_float_tys` when possible and otherwise creating one; explicitly calls `Ty::new_infer` on the fallback path.
Constructs a generic parameter type from its index and name by interning `TyKind::Param` with `tcx.mk_ty_from_kind`.
Constructs a bound type with the given de Bruijn index and bound variable; explicitly calls `Ty::new`.
Constructs a placeholder type from a `PlaceholderType`; explicitly calls `Ty::new`.

Constructs an error type carrying an existing `ErrorGuaranteed`; explicitly calls `Ty::new`.

Returns the canonical interned signed integer type from `tcx.types` for the requested `IntTy` variant.
Returns the canonical interned unsigned integer type from `tcx.types` for the requested `UintTy` variant.

Constructs a tuple type from a slice of element types. If the slice is empty it returns `tcx.types.unit`; otherwise it calls `tcx.mk_type_list` and then `Ty::new` with the `Tuple` variant.
Builds a tuple type from an iterator by calling `T::collect_and_apply`, which in turn invokes `Ty::new_tup` on the collected element types.

Constructs a function-definition type after asserting the `DefId` is a function-like item, calling `tcx.check_and_mk_args` to validate/build generic arguments, and then `Ty::new` with the `FnDef` variant.
Constructs a function-pointer type by calling `split` on the polymorphic signature and then `Ty::new` with the `FnPtr` variant.
Constructs a dynamic trait object type from existential predicates, region, and representation by calling `Ty::new` with the `Dynamic` variant.
Constructs a projection alias type from prebuilt generic arguments by calling `AliasTy::new_from_args` and then `Ty::new_alias` with `ty::Projection`.
Constructs a projection alias type from an argument iterator by calling `AliasTy::new` and then `Ty::new_alias` with `ty::Projection`.
Constructs a closure type after calling `tcx.debug_assert_args_compatible` to verify the captured generic arguments, then `Ty::new` with the `Closure` variant.
Constructs a coroutine-closure type after calling `tcx.debug_assert_args_compatible` to verify arguments, then `Ty::new` with the `CoroutineClosure` variant.
Constructs a coroutine type after calling `tcx.debug_assert_args_compatible` to verify arguments, then `Ty::new` with the `Coroutine` variant.
Constructs a coroutine-witness type by calling `Ty::new` with the `CoroutineWitness` variant.
Constructs the `&'static str` type by calling `Ty::new_imm_ref` with `tcx.lifetimes.re_static` and `tcx.types.str_`.
Returns the default fallback type for diverging expressions by calling `tcx.features()` and choosing `tcx.types.never` when `never_type_fallback` is enabled, otherwise `tcx.types.unit`.

Internal helper that constructs a single-type-parameter ADT wrapper. It calls `tcx.adt_def` to fetch the ADT, `GenericArgs::for_item` to build arguments, uses `tcx.type_of(...).instantiate(...)` for defaulted type parameters beyond the first, and finally calls `Ty::new` with the `Adt` variant.
Looks up a lang item type constructor via `tcx.lang_items().get` and, when found, calls `Ty::new_generic_adt` to build the instantiated ADT type.
Looks up a diagnostic item via `tcx.get_diagnostic_item` and, when found, calls `Ty::new_generic_adt` to build the instantiated ADT type.
Constructs `Box<T>` by calling `tcx.require_lang_item` for `LangItem::OwnedBox` and then `Ty::new_generic_adt` with the inner type.
Constructs `MaybeUninit<T>` by calling `tcx.require_lang_item` for `LangItem::MaybeUninit` and then `Ty::new_generic_adt` with the inner type.

Constructs the erased mutable reference type used for task contexts. It calls `tcx.require_lang_item` to find `Context`, `tcx.adt_def` to get its ADT, `tcx.mk_args` to create erased lifetime args, `Ty::new_adt` to build the context type, and `Ty::new_mut_ref` to wrap it in `&mut`.
Returns the canonical boolean type `tcx.types.bool` without calling other methods in the provided methods list.
Returns the canonical `u8` type `tcx.types.u8` without calling other methods in the provided methods list.
Delegates to `Ty::new_infer` to construct an inference type.
Delegates to `Ty::new_var` to construct a type variable.
Delegates to `Ty::new_param`, passing the parameter's index and name, to construct a generic parameter type.
Delegates to `Ty::new_placeholder` to construct a placeholder type.
Delegates to `Ty::new_bound` to construct a bound type from a Debruijn index and bound type descriptor.
Constructs an anonymous bound type by calling `Ty::new_bound` with a synthesized `ty::BoundTy` whose kind is `Anon`.
Delegates to `Ty::new_alias` to construct an alias type of the requested alias kind.
Trait adapter that constructs an error type by directly forwarding to `Ty::new_error`. Calls `new_error`.
Trait adapter that constructs an ADT type from an `AdtDef` and generic arguments by forwarding to `Ty::new_adt`. Calls `new_adt`.
Trait adapter that constructs a foreign type for the given `DefId` by forwarding to `Ty::new_foreign`. Calls `new_foreign`.
Trait adapter that constructs a dynamic trait object type from existential predicates, region, and dyn kind by forwarding to `Ty::new_dynamic`. Calls `new_dynamic`.
Trait adapter that constructs a coroutine type from its definition id and generic arguments by forwarding to `Ty::new_coroutine`. Calls `new_coroutine`.
Trait adapter that constructs a coroutine-closure type from its definition id and generic arguments by forwarding to `Ty::new_coroutine_closure`. Calls `new_coroutine_closure`.
Trait adapter that constructs a closure type from its definition id and generic arguments by forwarding to `Ty::new_closure`. Calls `new_closure`.
Trait adapter that constructs a coroutine witness type from its definition id and generic arguments by forwarding to `Ty::new_coroutine_witness`. Calls `new_coroutine_witness`.
Trait adapter that constructs a raw pointer type for an element type and mutability by forwarding to `Ty::new_ptr`. Calls `new_ptr`.
Trait adapter that constructs a reference type from a region, pointee type, and mutability by forwarding to `Ty::new_ref`. Calls `new_ref`.
Trait adapter that constructs an array type with a constant length by forwarding to `Ty::new_array_with_const_len`. Calls `new_array_with_const_len`.
Trait adapter that constructs a slice type for the given element type by forwarding to `Ty::new_slice`. Calls `new_slice`.
Trait adapter that constructs a tuple type from a slice of element types by forwarding to `Ty::new_tup`. Calls `new_tup`.
Trait adapter that constructs a tuple type from an iterator using the collection/apply abstraction by forwarding to `Ty::new_tup_from_iter`. Calls `new_tup_from_iter`.
Trait adapter that returns the element types of a tuple by delegating to the inherent tuple-field accessor on `Ty`. Calls `tuple_fields`.
Trait adapter that interprets the type as an optional closure kind by delegating to the inherent `Ty` helper. Calls `to_opt_closure_kind`.
Trait adapter that converts a closure kind into its corresponding type representation by forwarding to `Ty::from_closure_kind`. Calls `from_closure_kind`.
Trait adapter that converts a coroutine-closure kind into its corresponding type representation by forwarding to `Ty::from_coroutine_closure_kind`. Calls `from_coroutine_closure_kind`.
Trait adapter that constructs a function-definition type from a `DefId` and generic arguments by forwarding to `Ty::new_fn_def`. Calls `new_fn_def`.
Trait adapter that constructs a function-pointer type from a bound function signature by forwarding to `Ty::new_fn_ptr`. Calls `new_fn_ptr`.
Trait adapter that constructs a pattern-refined type from a base type and pattern by forwarding to `Ty::new_pat`. Calls `new_pat`.
Returns the canonical unit type from `TyCtxt`'s preinterned common types.
Returns the canonical `usize` type from `TyCtxt`'s preinterned common types.
Trait adapter that computes the discriminant type for this type by delegating to the inherent `Ty` helper. Calls `discriminant_ty`.
Trait adapter that computes the async-destructor type associated with this type by delegating to the inherent `Ty` helper. Calls `async_destructor_ty`.
Returns the interned `TyKind` backing this `Ty` by directly exposing the stored representation.
Returns the cached `TypeFlags` stored on the underlying interned type representation.
Checks whether the type is the unit type by matching on `self.kind()` and testing whether the tuple field list is empty. Calls `kind`.
Checks whether the type is the `!` never type by matching on `self.kind()`. Calls `kind`.
Checks whether the type is a primitive scalar-like built-in type (`bool`, `char`, integer, unsigned integer, or float) by matching on `self.kind()`. Calls `kind`.
Returns whether the type’s kind is `Adt`; calls `kind` to inspect the underlying `TyKind`.
Returns whether the type’s kind is `Ref`; calls `kind` to inspect the underlying `TyKind`.
Returns whether the type is an inference type variable `Infer(TyVar(_))`; calls `kind` to inspect the type kind.
Extracts the `TyVid` from an inference type variable and returns it as `Some`, or `None` otherwise; calls `kind` to pattern-match the type kind.
Returns whether the type is any inference kind `Infer(_)`, including type or numeric inference; calls `kind` to inspect the type kind.
Returns whether the type is an ADT whose definition is `PhantomData`; calls `kind` to obtain the ADT and then calls the ADT definition’s `is_phantom_data`.
Returns whether the type kind is exactly `Bool`; calls `kind` to inspect the type kind.
Returns whether the type kind is exactly `Str`; calls `kind` to inspect the type kind.
Returns whether the type is a generic parameter with the given index; calls `kind` to match `Param` and compare its stored index.
Returns whether the type’s kind is `Slice`; calls `kind` to inspect the type kind.
Returns whether the type is a slice directly, or a raw/reference pointer to a slice; calls `kind` on `self`, and for pointer/reference cases also calls `kind` on the pointee type.
Returns whether the type’s kind is `Array`; calls `kind` to inspect the type kind.
Returns whether the type is an ADT with SIMD representation; calls `kind` to match `Adt`, then calls `repr` and `simd` on the ADT definition.
Returns the element type of an `Array` or `Slice`, or `u8` for `str`; calls `kind` to inspect the sequence kind and otherwise errors on non-sequence types.

Extracts the lane count and lane element type from a SIMD ADT by validating its representation and unpacking its single array field; calls `kind` on `self`, calls `repr` and `simd` on the ADT definition, calls `non_enum_variant`, `len`, and the field definition’s `ty`, then calls `kind` on the field type and finally calls `eval_target_usize` with `ParamEnv::empty` to compute the array length.
Returns whether the type is a mutable raw pointer or mutable reference; calls `kind` to inspect the type kind.
Returns the mutability if the type is a reference, or `None` otherwise; calls `kind` to match `Ref` and extract its mutability.
Returns whether the type is a raw pointer; calls `kind` to inspect the type kind.
Returns whether the type is any pointer-like type accepted here: reference, raw pointer, or function pointer; explicitly calls `is_ref`, `is_unsafe_ptr`, and `is_fn_ptr`.
Returns whether the type is the `Box` ADT; calls `kind` to match `Adt`, then calls the ADT definition’s `is_box`.

Returns whether the type is a `Box` using the global allocator, treating one-argument `Box` as global for minicore; calls `kind`, the ADT definition’s `is_box`, argument list `get`, `expect_ty`, `ty_adt_def`, `is_some_and`, `tcx.require_lang_item`, and the allocator ADT’s `did` for comparison.
Returns the boxed inner type for a `Box` ADT, or `None` otherwise; calls `kind`, the ADT definition’s `is_box`, and `type_at(0)` on the generic arguments.
Returns the boxed inner type and panics if the type is not `Box`; explicitly calls `boxed_ty` and then `unwrap_or_else` to report misuse.

Returns whether the type is one of the scalar kinds recognized here: primitive integers/floats/chars/bool, function items/pointers, raw pointers, or numeric inference variables; calls `kind` to inspect the type kind.
Returns whether the type is a floating-point type or floating-point inference variable; calls `kind` to inspect the type kind.
Returns whether the type is a `dyn Trait` object (not `dyn*`); calls `kind` to match `Dynamic(..., ty::Dyn)`.
Returns whether the type is a `dyn*` trait object; calls `kind` to match `Dynamic(..., ty::DynStar)`.
Returns whether the type is an ADT whose definition is an enum; calls `kind` to match `Adt` and then calls the ADT definition’s `is_enum`.
Returns whether the type is an ADT whose definition is a union; calls `kind` to match `Adt` and then calls the ADT definition’s `is_union`.
Returns whether the type’s kind is `Closure`; calls `kind` to inspect the type kind.
Returns whether this type is a coroutine by inspecting `self.kind()` for the `Coroutine(..)` variant.
Returns whether this type is a coroutine closure by inspecting `self.kind()` for the `CoroutineClosure(..)` variant.
Returns whether this type is an integral type, accepting integer inference vars and concrete signed/unsigned integer kinds via `self.kind()`.
Returns whether this type is specifically a fresh type inference variable by matching `self.kind()` against `Infer(FreshTy(_))`.
Returns whether this type is any fresh inference type by matching `self.kind()` against fresh type, fresh int, or fresh float inference variants.
Returns whether this type is `char` by checking `self.kind()` for `Char`.
Returns whether this type is numeric. Calls `is_integral` and `is_floating_point`, succeeding if either predicate is true.
Returns whether this type is a signed integer by matching `self.kind()` against `Int(_)`.
Returns whether this type is a pointer-sized integer by matching `self.kind()` against `isize` or `usize`.
Returns whether the type has a concrete outer shape, rejecting parameter, inference, and error kinds based on `self.kind()`.

Checks whether `self` contains `other` anywhere in its type structure. Calls `visit_with` with a local `ContainsTyVisitor`, whose `visit_ty` compares each visited type and otherwise calls `super_visit_with`; the final result is tested with `is_break()`.
Visitor step for `contains`: breaks when the current type equals the searched-for type, otherwise calls `t.super_visit_with(self)` to keep traversing nested types.

Checks whether `self` contains any closure type. Calls `visit_with` with a local `ContainsClosureVisitor`, whose `visit_ty` inspects `t.kind()` for `Closure(..)` and otherwise calls `super_visit_with`; the search result is returned via `is_break()`.
Visitor step for `contains_closure`: checks `t.kind()` for `ty::Closure(..)`, returns `Break` when found, and otherwise calls `t.super_visit_with(self)` to recurse.
Returns the builtin dereference target type if one exists. Calls `boxed_ty` first, then falls back to matching `self.kind()` for references and, when `explicit` is true, raw pointers.
Returns the element type for builtin indexing by matching `self.kind()` as an array or slice.

Computes the callable signature for function-like types. It matches `self.kind()`, calling `tcx.fn_sig(*def_id).instantiate(tcx, args)` for `FnDef`, `with` for `FnPtr`, producing `Binder::dummy(...)` with `ty::List::empty()` for `Error`, and rejecting closures/non-functions with `bug!`.
Returns whether this type is a function item or function pointer by matching `self.kind()` against `FnDef(..)` or `FnPtr(..)`.
Returns whether this type is a function pointer by matching `self.kind()` against `FnPtr(..)`.
Returns whether this type is an opaque `impl Trait` by matching `self.kind()` against `Alias(ty::Opaque, ..)`.
Returns the underlying ADT definition when `self.kind()` is `Adt`, otherwise `None`.
Returns the tuple field list by matching `self.kind()` as `Tuple`; otherwise it panics with `bug!` for non-tuples.
Returns the valid variant index range for ADTs and coroutines. For coroutines it explicitly calls `args.as_coroutine().variant_range(*def_id, tcx)`; for ADTs it uses the ADT's `variant_range()`.

Returns the discriminant value for a given variant on enums or coroutines. For enums it calls `adt.discriminant_for_variant(tcx, variant_index)`, and for coroutines it calls `args.as_coroutine().discriminant_for_variant(*def_id, tcx, variant_index)`.

Computes the discriminant type for this type. It calls `adt.repr().discr_type().to_ty(tcx)` for enums, `args.as_coroutine().discr_ty(tcx)` for coroutines, builds a `DiscriminantKind` projection using `require_lang_item`, `associated_item_def_ids`, `mk_args`, and `new_projection_from_args` for param/alias/type-var cases, recursively calls `ty.discriminant_ty(tcx)` for `Pat`, returns `tcx.types.u8` for the remaining concrete cases, and `bug!`s on unexpected bound/placeholder/fresh inference kinds.

Builds the async destructor type for `self`. It first calls `async_drop_glue_morphology`; for `Noop` and `DeferredDropInPlace` it constructs combinators using `async_destructor_combinator`, `instantiate_identity`, and `instantiate`. For custom cases it matches `self.kind()`: param/alias/type-var builds an `AsyncDestruct` projection via `require_lang_item`, `associated_item_def_ids`, and `new_projection`; arrays/slices compose `AsyncDropSlice` and `AsyncDropFuse`; structs/enums, tuples, closures, and coroutine closures delegate to `adt_async_destructor_ty` (using `as_closure().upvar_tys()` or `as_coroutine_closure().upvar_tys()` where relevant); unions call `surface_async_dropper_ty` and then wrap the result with `AsyncDropFuse`.

Helper for assembling an async destructor over ADT-like variant/field layouts. It calls `async_drop_glue_morphology` for a debug assertion, obtains combinator types via `async_destructor_combinator`, folds each field list into chained deferred destructors with `instantiate`, reduces variants with `AsyncDropEither`, optionally prepends `surface_async_dropper_ty`, and finally wraps the result with `AsyncDropFuse` using `instantiate`.

Returns the surface-level async dropper type for an ADT if it has an async destructor or normal destructor. It calls `ty_adt_def`, then queries `async_destructor` and `destructor`, and finally builds the combinator with `async_destructor_combinator(...).instantiate(tcx, &[self.into()])`.

Looks up the output type of an async-drop lang-item combinator function. It calls `tcx.require_lang_item`, then `tcx.fn_sig(...)`, and maps the bound signature with `map_bound` by extracting `fn_sig.output().no_bound_vars().unwrap()`.

Determines pointer metadata for the unsized tail of `self`, or returns the unresolved tail when metadata depends on it. It first calls `tcx.struct_tail_raw(self, normalize, || {})`, then matches `tail.kind()`: sized tails return `Ok(tcx.types.unit)`, `str`/slice return `Ok(tcx.types.usize)`, dyn trait objects call `require_lang_item`, `type_of`, and `instantiate` to produce `DynMetadata<tail>`, param/alias tails return `Err(tail)`, and unexpected inference/bound/pattern forms trigger `bug!`.
Returns the pointee metadata type for `self`, delegating to `ptr_metadata_ty_or_tail`; if that helper returns `Err`, it aborts with `bug!` instead of propagating the unsized tail.

Computes the metadata type for the pointee of a pointer/reference type. It calls `builtin_deref` to extract the pointee, `is_trivially_sized` to treat sized pointees as `()`, and `ptr_metadata_ty_or_tail` to obtain concrete metadata; if only an unsized tail is available, it uses `tcx.lang_items().metadata_type()` and `Ty::new_projection` to build the corresponding metadata projection type.

Interprets the type as the internal integer encoding of a closure kind. It calls `kind` to inspect the `TyKind`, mapping `i8/i16/i32` to `Fn/FnMut/FnOnce`, returning `None` for unresolved generic/bound forms, and `bug!` for unsupported concrete kinds.
Constructs the internal type encoding for a closure kind by mapping `Fn`, `FnMut`, and `FnOnce` to `tcx.types.i8`, `i16`, and `i32` respectively.
Constructs the internal type encoding for a coroutine-closure kind, mapping `Fn` and `FnMut` to `tcx.types.i16` and `FnOnce` to `tcx.types.i32`.

Checks whether the type is obviously sized without normalization or trait solving. It calls `kind` to classify the type, recursively calls `is_trivially_sized` on the last element of tuples, and for ADTs calls `sized_constraint`, `instantiate`, and then `is_trivially_sized` on the instantiated constraint; aliases, params, placeholders, bounds, and unresolved type vars are conservatively treated as not trivially sized.

Checks whether the type is an obviously trivial, pure `Clone`/`Copy` case. It calls `kind` to inspect the type, recursively calls `is_trivially_pure_clone_copy` for array elements and pattern inner types, and for small tuples uses `iter().all(Self::is_trivially_pure_clone_copy)` to require every field to satisfy the same predicate; most structured, normalized, or uncertain cases are conservatively rejected.

Returns the diagnostic symbol for primitive scalar types. It calls `kind` and maps boolean, character, integer, and float `TyKind`s to their corresponding `sym::*` name, returning `None` for non-primitive types.
Checks whether the type is the `c_void` lang item. It calls `kind` to detect an ADT, then calls `adt.did()` and `tcx.is_lang_item(..., LangItem::CVoid)` to test the definition identity.

Determines whether the type is a rigid, fully known structural `TyKind` rather than an inference, alias, parameter, bound, placeholder, or error form. It calls `kind` and returns `true` only for concrete type constructors like scalars, ADTs, pointers, refs, functions, closures, coroutines, `str`, arrays, slices, tuples, and `never`.

Returns the function input types from a `List<Ty>` that stores inputs followed by output. It calls `split_last` to separate the final output type and `unwrap` to assume the list is non-empty, then returns the input slice.

Returns the function output type from a `List<Ty>` that stores inputs followed by output. It calls `split_last` to obtain the final element and `unwrap` to assume the list is non-empty, then returns that last type.
method_docs.compiler/rustc_ast_lowering/src/expr.rs:: Lowers a slice of AST expressions into an arena-allocated HIR slice by iterating over the input and calling `lower_expr_mut` for each element.
Public helper that lowers one AST expression and arena-allocates the result; it calls `lower_expr_mut` to perform the actual lowering.

Main expression-lowering dispatcher that matches on `ExprKind` and builds the corresponding HIR node, including desugarings and diagnostics for special forms. In the shown portion it explicitly calls `lower_expr`, `lower_exprs`, `lower_anon_const`, `lower_array_length`, `lower_node_id`, `lower_span`, `lower_legacy_const_generics`, `lower_path_segment`, `lower_binop`, `lower_unop`, and `lower_ty`.
Converts an AST unary operator directly into the corresponding HIR unary operator without calling other methods from the list.
Converts an AST binary operator into a HIR `BinOp`, preserving its span by calling `lower_span`.

Rewrites a call using legacy const-generic argument positions into a normal generic call by splitting const and value arguments, attaching synthesized generic args to the path, then calling `lower_expr` for the callee and `lower_exprs` for the remaining runtime arguments.
Lowers an `if` expression by calling `lower_cond` for the condition, `lower_block_expr` for the then-block, and `lower_expr` for the optional else-expression.

Lowers a condition expression while preserving the special temporary-lifetime behavior of `let` chains. It calls the local helper `has_let_expr`, and depending on the form calls `lower_binop`, `lower_cond` recursively, `lower_expr`, `mark_span_with_reason`, and `expr_drop_temps`.
Local recursive helper that checks whether an expression tree contains any `let` expression by recursively inspecting binary subexpressions and calling itself on both operands.

Desugars a `while` loop into an HIR `loop` containing an `if` whose else branch breaks. It calls `lower_cond` inside `with_loop_condition_scope`, `lower_block_expr`, `expr_break`, `stmt_expr`, `block_all`, `expr_block`, `expr`, `block_expr`, `lower_span`, and `lower_label`.

Desugars a `try { ... }` block by lowering the block body under a catch scope, wrapping the tail expression with the `Try::from_output` constructor, and returning it as a block expression. It calls `with_catch_scope`, `lower_block_noalloc`, `mark_span_with_reason`, `expr_unit`, and `wrap_in_try_constructor`.
Builds a call to a lang-item constructor around an already-lowered expression; it calls `expr_lang_item_path` to create the callee and `expr_call` to invoke it.

Lowers a match arm, including its pattern, optional guard, attributes, body, and span. It calls `lower_pat`, `lower_span`, `next_id`, `lower_expr`, and `lower_attrs`, and for `if let` guards it calls `lower_pat` and `lower_expr` again to build the lowered `hir::Let`.

Builds the HIR expression kind for a desugared coroutine/async construct by setting up the coroutine kind, synthesized resume/task-context parameters for async forms, the return type, and the lowered closure/coroutine body. It explicitly calls `local_def_id`, `mark_span_with_reason`, `lower_span`, `make_lang_item_qpath`, `next_id`, `pat_ident_binding_mode`, `with_def_id_parent`, and `lower_body`.

Checks whether `async_fn_track_caller` is enabled and the outer HIR node has a `#[track_caller]` attribute; if so, it marks the span as an async desugaring span and forwards a synthesized `#[track_caller]` attribute onto the inner HIR node. Calls `mark_span_with_reason` to adjust the span and `lower_attrs` to attach the generated attribute.

Desugars `.await` into the polling loop over a future, including context access, pinning, poll matching, yielding pending, and breaking with the ready value; it also emits an error outside async contexts. In the shown body it calls `mark_span_with_reason`, `lower_expr_mut`, `pat_ident_binding_mode`, `expr_ident`, `expr_mut_addr_of`, `expr_ident_mut`, `expr_err`, `expr_call_lang_item_fn_mut`, `expr_call_lang_item_fn`, `expr_unsafe`, `next_node_id`, `lower_node_id`, `pat_ident`, `single_pat_field`, `pat_lang_item_variant`, `with_loop_scope`, `lower_loop_destination`, `expr`, `arm`, `expr_block_empty`, `expr_match`, `stmt_expr`, `expr_unit`, `lower_span`, `stmt`, and `block_all`.

Desugars an `.await` expression into the corresponding HIR control-flow structure, including validation that await appears in an async context, creation of temporary bindings, polling/yielding logic, and an error block fallback when used outside async code. It explicitly calls `next_id`, `dcx`, `block_all`, `mark_span_with_reason`, `pat_ident_binding_mode`, `expr_ident`, `expr_mut_addr_of`, `expr_ident_mut`, `expr_call_lang_item_fn_mut`, `expr_call_lang_item_fn`, `expr_unsafe`, `next_node_id`, `lower_node_id`, `pat_ident`, `single_pat_field`, `pat_lang_item_variant`, `with_loop_scope`, `lower_loop_destination`, `arm`, `expr_block_empty`, `expr_match`, `stmt_expr`, `expr_lang_item_path`, `expr_unit`, and `lower_span`.

Lowers a closure expression by lowering its binder, body, generator metadata, generic params, and function declaration, then assembling a HIR closure node. It calls `lower_closure_binder`, `with_new_scopes`, `lower_fn_body`, `lower_expr_mut`, `generator_movability_for_fn`, `lower_lifetime_binder`, `lower_fn_decl`, and `lower_span`.

Determines the resulting `hir::ClosureKind` for a function-like expression from its coroutine kind and movability, emitting diagnostics for invalid coroutine parameter counts or `static` non-coroutine closures. It explicitly calls `dcx` to emit those errors.
Lowers a closure binder into its HIR form and returns the associated generic parameters slice, calling `lower_span` when a `for<...>` binder is present.

Lowers an async coroutine closure expression by creating the closure def-id/binder, lowering an inner moved-argument coroutine body within fresh scopes, forwarding `track_caller`, lowering generic lifetime binders and the function declaration, and finally constructing the HIR closure node as a coroutine closure. It explicitly calls `local_def_id`, `lower_closure_binder`, `with_new_scopes`, `with_def_id_parent`, `lower_body`, `lower_coroutine_body_with_moved_arguments`, `lower_expr_mut`, `maybe_forward_track_caller`, `lower_lifetime_binder`, `lower_fn_decl`, and `lower_span`.

Lowers assignment expressions, using plain HIR assignment for ordinary lvalues and desugaring destructuring assignment into a temporary `let` plus per-place assignments otherwise. It calls the local helper `is_ordinary`, and for destructuring paths calls `lower_expr`, `lower_span`, `destructure_assign`, `stmt_let_pat`, and `block_all`.

Local recursive helper that decides whether an assignment lhs is a normal assignable place or needs destructuring desugaring; it calls `extract_tuple_struct_path` for call expressions and calls itself recursively through parenthesized expressions.
Checks whether an expression is a path usable as a tuple-struct or tuple-variant pattern and returns its `qself`/path pair if so; it does not call other methods from the list.
Checks whether an expression is a path usable as a unit-struct or unit-variant pattern and returns its `qself`/path pair if so; it does not call other methods from the list.
Convenience wrapper that lowers a destructuring-assignment lhs into an arena-allocated HIR pattern by calling `destructure_assign_mut`.

Recursively lowers a destructuring-assignment lhs into a mutable HIR pattern and records side-effecting assignment statements for bound places.
